title: Deeper/broader cross-peer fix provenance and writer-boundary refresh
mode: primary-source issue/commit research and scoped local source audit
scope: Reconcile current LibreDWG DXF-writer issue reports with linked commits and mutable master source
Check whether LibreDWG's quoted-string buffer defect has an equivalent in the local DXF text sink
Reconcile recent ACadSharp reader/writer reports with existing local plan owners and evidence grades
Refine implementation readiness without changing the local implementation queue or validation cadence

method.kind: Read-only review of primary project issues, commits, current source, and existing local plan/source/test ownership
method.limitations: Issue bodies and mutable default-branch source describe their cited state, not every release artifact. ACadSharp issue #1282 was visible only as an issue-index title in this pass. Local writer review was scoped to the direct text sinks and nearby encoding/chunk helpers; it was not a sanitizer run or exhaustive memory-safety proof. No peer drawing or issue attachment was acquired.

sources.revision: issue body and activity reviewed 2026-10-18; issue page showed Open
sources.observed: The report describes a C DXF string quoting buffer whose actual written end was not NUL-terminated before strlen, allowing unwritten heap bytes into output. It also describes a latent zero-length transformed-value case that could omit the entire group. The issue page lists two commits referencing the report.
Adds termination at the last byte written by cquote, clamped within the buffer; it is a commit-level fix, not by itself a tagged-release qualification.
Adds explicit empty group output in dxf_write_chunked when the transformed string length is zero. The commit describes this as hardening for a state not reproduced in its master tests.
Current source contains both the cquote written-end terminator and the dxf_write_chunked zero-length group guard. This does not prove a particular formal release contains either change.
The report identifies NOD physical ordering as distinct from handle order and is already mapped to the local root-ordering plan/test owner.

#1414 leaves the source TV/TU versus target-DXF Unicode escape policy unresolved; #1415 reports method/index confusion in CMC handling. Both are already mapped to local text-route and method-discriminated color evidence.

#1281, #1279, #1280, and #1297 provide detailed failure-mode reports; #1282 was visible only by index title; #1299 depends on an attached drawing not reviewed here. Their reports map to existing local robustness, text, graph, and spline evidence owners but do not establish local defects. #1297 specifically reports whole-file rejection despite a reportedly identical MTEXT body, while its proposed cause remains unproven.

localAudit.directSinkReview: dxfWriterAscii::writeString writes the supplied string_view data for exactly its size. dxfWriterBinary::writeStringImpl writes the supplied view length for ordinary strings; binary payload chunks are separately length-checked. Nearby UTF-8 conversion retains owned std::string storage and chunk emission uses explicit offsets/sizes.
localAudit.auditLimit: Scoped static inspection only; not an exhaustive audit of every conversion/helper path and not dynamic memory-safety validation.
localAudit.testOwnerDisposition: Reuse existing writer/text owners if a future local change adds a mutable, length-changing buffer. Existing generated encoding and chunk tests remain in place; no test added in this research pass.

assessment.planImpact: Adds a conditional invariant for future mutable-buffer text transforms, clarifies that issue status/current master/released artifacts are separate evidence, and reinforces whole-file acceptance after entity-level body checks. Existing local owners and implementation order are unchanged.

implementationReadyChecks: Continue the dependency-ready local implementation queue; do not wait on a peer issue or branch state.

For a future mutable-buffer string transform, track the initialized output length, terminate at that boundary where required, preserve explicit empty group records, and assert a following typed sentinel in the existing writer test owner.

Keep per-slice validation to the touched strict target, focused generated selector, compatibility check, and owning CTest; run sanitizers/allocator-noise/fuzzing only at the existing scheduled or composed security checkpoint.
Pin the exact peer source commit and release/package separately; do not transfer current-master fixes to a release without ancestry or artifact evidence.
Retain file-level inventory, object/reference closure, strict independent readback, and native acceptance after entity-body checks; keep unavailable gates non-blocking for local implementation.
